flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Axial Electric Field of Charged Ring
flipcards.prompt: Electric field on the axis of a uniformly charged ring of radius R at distance x from center
flipcards.vars: q = charge (or Nq = total charge), R = ring radius, x = axial distance, k = 1/(4πε₀)
flipcards.tip: Maximum at x = ±R/√2; for x ≫ R, behaves like a point charge kQ/x²

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Tension in Charged Ring Due to Central Charge
flipcards.prompt: Tension T in a ring of linear charge density λ and radius R with charge q at its center
flipcards.vars: q = central charge, λ = linear charge density of ring, R = radius, k = 1/(4πε₀)
flipcards.tip: Derived from radial force balance: 2T sin(dθ/2) = (kq λ R dθ)/R²

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Force Between Charged Rod and Point Charge
flipcards.prompt: Force by a uniformly charged rod (length l, charge Q) on point charge q at distance a from near end
flipcards.vars: Q = rod charge, q = point charge, a = distance from near end, l = rod length
flipcards.tip: Effective distance is the geometric mean √(a(a+l))

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Two Charged Pendulums in Equilibrium
flipcards.prompt: Find charge q when tan θ = Fe / mg for small angles (separation x, string length l)
flipcards.vars: x = separation, m = mass, l = string length, k = 1/(4πε₀)
flipcards.tip: Valid for small θ where tan θ ≈ sin θ = x/(2l)

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Charged Pendulum in Dielectric Liquid
flipcards.prompt: Relation between weight mg, buoyant force B, and dielectric constant K when θ stays unchanged
flipcards.vars: K = dielectric constant, B = buoyant force, m = mass of bob
flipcards.tip: From Fe/mg = (Fe/K)/(mg − B); gives K = ρ_body / (ρ_body − ρ_liq)

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Electric Flux Through a Circular Disk
flipcards.prompt: Electric flux from a point charge q passing through a disk subtending half-angle θ at q
flipcards.vars: q = point charge, θ = half-angle of cone formed by disk rim at charge
flipcards.tip: Solid angle of a cone is Ω = 2π(1 − cos θ); Φ = qΩ/(4πɛ₀)

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Electric Field Inside Solid Sphere
flipcards.prompt: Electric field at distance r ≤ R inside a uniformly charged solid non-conducting sphere
flipcards.vars: ρ = volume charge density, Q = total charge, R = sphere radius, r = distance from center
flipcards.tip: E ∝ r inside (zero at center) and maximum at surface r = R

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Electric Field Outside Hollow Long Cylinder
flipcards.prompt: Electric field at distance r ≥ R outside a uniformly charged long hollow cylinder
flipcards.vars: σ = surface charge density, R = cylinder radius, r = perpendicular distance from axis
flipcards.tip: Inside the hollow cylinder (r < R), E = 0

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Electric Field of Solid Long Cylinder
flipcards.prompt: Electric field inside (r ≤ R) and outside/on (r ≥ R) a uniformly charged solid long cylinder
flipcards.vars: ρ = volume charge density, R = cylinder radius, r = perpendicular distance from axis
flipcards.tip: Inside E ∝ r; outside E ∝ 1/r

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Electric Field Inside Cavity (Sphere & Cylinder)
flipcards.prompt: Uniform electric field inside a spherical or cylindrical cavity with centers/axes at r₁ and r₂
flipcards.vars: ρ = volume charge density, r₁ − r₂ = vector from body center/axis to cavity center/axis
flipcards.tip: Field is completely uniform inside the cavity and independent of cavity radius

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Speed Leaving a Spherical Dome
flipcards.prompt: Velocity of a particle sliding frictionlessly from the top of a spherical dome when it loses contact
flipcards.vars: g = gravitational acceleration, R = radius of spherical dome
flipcards.tip: Loser of contact occurs at height h = R/3 below the top (cos θ = 2/3)

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Spring Rest-to-Rest Elongation
flipcards.prompt: Maximum extension L when a block of mass m is released from rest from natural length of a vertical spring
flipcards.vars: m = mass, g = gravity, k = spring constant
flipcards.tip: Equilibrium extension is mg/k; maximum (rest-to-rest) extension is double that: 2mg/k

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Electric Field Due to Infinite Sheet
flipcards.prompt: Electric field near an infinite non-conducting plane sheet of surface charge density σ
flipcards.vars: σ = surface charge density (C/m²)
flipcards.tip: Independent of distance from the sheet; for a conducting plate, E = σ/ε₀

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Electric Field Between R₁ and R₂ of Thick Shell
flipcards.prompt: Electric field at r (R₁ < r < R₂) inside a thick spherical shell (or cylindrical shell)
flipcards.latex: E_{\text{sph}} = \frac{\rho(r^3 - R_1^3)}{3\varepsilon_0 r^2} \quad | \quad E_{\text{cyl}} = \frac{\rho(r^2 - R_1^2)}{2\varepsilon_0 r}
flipcards.vars: ρ = volume charge density, R₁ = inner radius, R₂ = outer radius, r = distance from center/axis
flipcards.tip: Enclosed charge for sphere uses 4π(r³ − R₁³)/3; for cylinder uses π(r² − R₁²)L

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Galvanometer to Voltmeter & Ammeter
flipcards.prompt: Series resistance R_s for Voltmeter (range V) and Shunt S for Ammeter (range I)
flipcards.latex: V = I_g(R_g + R_s) \quad | \quad I_g R_g = (I - I_g)S
flipcards.vars: I_g = full-scale deflection current, R_g = galvanometer resistance, R_s = high series R, S = low shunt R
flipcards.tip: Voltmeter connects in parallel (high R_s); Ammeter connects in series (low S)

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Equivalent Resistance of a Frustum
flipcards.prompt: Resistance along the axis of a conical frustum of length L and end radii R₁, R₂
flipcards.vars: ρ = resistivity, L = length, R₁ & R₂ = end radii
flipcards.tip: Uses geometric mean cross-section area π R₁ R₂

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Radial Resistance Between Concentric Spheres
flipcards.prompt: Equivalent radial resistance between two concentric spherical shells of radii R₁ and R₂ (R₂ > R₁)
flipcards.vars: ρ = resistivity of medium, R₁ = inner radius, R₂ = outer radius
flipcards.tip: Derived by integrating dR = ρ dr / (4πr²) from R₁ to R₂

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Polarized Charge & Density in Dielectric
flipcards.prompt: Induced surface charge density σ_p and induced charge q_p on a dielectric slab (constant K)
flipcards.vars: σ₀ = free charge density, K = dielectric constant, C = capacitance with dielectric
flipcards.tip: Wait: if C₀ is air capacitance and V is constant, free charge is K C₀ V, so q_p = C₀ V (K − 1)

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Work Done by Battery on Inserting Dielectric
flipcards.prompt: Work done by a constant-voltage battery V when a dielectric of constant K fills a capacitor C
flipcards.vars: K = dielectric constant, C = initial air capacitance, V = battery voltage
flipcards.tip: Half of W_b increases stored energy ΔU = ½(K−1)CV², half is mechanical work/heat

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Capacitance of Spherical Capacitor
flipcards.prompt: Capacitance between concentric spheres of inner radius R₁ and outer radius R₂ (dielectric K)
flipcards.vars: K = dielectric constant, k = 1/(4πε₀), R₁ = inner radius, R₂ = outer radius
flipcards.tip: If R₂ → ∞ (isolated sphere), C = 4πε₀ K R₁

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Axial Resistance of Hollow Cylinder
flipcards.prompt: Equivalent resistance along the axis of a hollow cylinder (length L, radii R₁ < R₂)
flipcards.vars: ρ = resistivity, L = length, R₁ = inner radius, R₂ = outer radius
flipcards.tip: Cross-sectional area is annular ring π(R₂² − R₁²)

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: RC Circuit Charging & Discharging
flipcards.prompt: Charge Q(t) on a capacitor during charging (EMF E) and discharging (initial charge Q₀)
flipcards.vars: τ = RC (time constant), E = battery EMF, Q₀ = initial charge
flipcards.tip: At t = τ, charging reaches 63.2% of max; discharging drops to 36.8% of Q₀

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Microscopic Resistance, Drift Speed & J
flipcards.prompt: Express resistance R, drift velocity v_d, and current density J in terms of relaxation time τ
flipcards.latex: R = \frac{m l}{n e^2 \tau A} \quad | \quad v_d = \frac{e E \tau}{m} \quad | \quad \vec{J} = \sigma\vec{E}
flipcards.vars: n = free electron density, τ = relaxation time, m = electron mass, σ = ne²τ/m
flipcards.tip: Resistivity ρ = m / (n e² τ); as temperature rises, τ decreases so ρ increases for metals

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Dimensions of Magnetic Flux
flipcards.prompt: Write the dimensional formula of magnetic flux Φ
flipcards.vars: Φ = B · A = (F / IL) · A = Work / Current
flipcards.tip: Quick check: Energy [ML²T⁻²] divided by Current [A] gives [ML²T⁻²A⁻¹]

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Magnetic Permeability of a Medium
flipcards.prompt: Relate absolute permeability μ of a medium to relative permeability μ_r
flipcards.vars: μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A (permeability of free space), μ_r = relative permeability
flipcards.tip: Also μ_r = 1 + χ_m, where χ_m is magnetic susceptibility

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Motional EMF Rod Braking: Velocity vs Time
flipcards.prompt: Velocity v(t) of a conducting rod (mass m, length L) sliding on rails (resistance R) in field B
flipcards.vars: u = initial velocity, B = magnetic field, L = rod length, R = loop resistance, m = mass
flipcards.tip: Exponential decay with time constant τ = Rm / (B²L²)

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Motional EMF Rod Braking: Velocity vs Distance
flipcards.prompt: Velocity v(x) as a function of distance x for a conducting rod braking in a magnetic field
flipcards.vars: u = initial velocity, x = distance traveled, B = field, L = length, R = resistance, m = mass
flipcards.tip: Maximum stopping distance when v = 0 is x_max = uRm / (B²L²)

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Magnetic Flux in Expanding Triangular Loop
flipcards.prompt: Magnetic flux Φ through an equilateral triangular loop expanding at speed v at time t
flipcards.vars: B = uniform magnetic field, v = speed of moving wire/vertex, t = time
flipcards.tip: Differentiate Φ w.r.t. t to get induced EMF: E = 2Bv²t / √3

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Motional EMF (General Vector Form)
flipcards.prompt: Motional EMF induced across a straight conductor of vector length L moving with velocity v in field B
flipcards.vars: v = velocity vector, B = magnetic field vector, L = length vector of conductor
flipcards.tip: If any two of v, B, L are parallel (or all three are coplanar), E = 0

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Induced Electric Field & Self-Induced EMF
flipcards.prompt: Induced E inside (r ≤ R) and outside (r ≥ R) a cylindrical region of changing B, plus inductor EMF
flipcards.vars: dB/dt = rate of change of magnetic field, R = field region radius, L = self-inductance
flipcards.tip: Induced E forms closed circular loops and is non-conservative

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: RL Circuit Current Growth & Time Constant
flipcards.prompt: Current i(t) during growth in a series RL circuit and its time constant τ
flipcards.vars: i₀ = E / R (steady-state current), L = inductance, R = resistance, τ = time constant
flipcards.tip: For current decay without battery: i = i₀ e^(−t/τ)

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Inductor Behavior at t = 0 and t → ∞
flipcards.prompt: How does an initially uncharged ideal inductor behave at t = 0 and in steady state (t → ∞)?
flipcards.vars: Applies to an ideal inductor with zero internal resistance
flipcards.tip: Opposite of an uncharged capacitor (capacitor is short at t = 0, open at t → ∞)

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Induced Charge Flow
flipcards.prompt: Total charge ΔQ flowing through a closed loop of resistance R when magnetic flux changes by ΔΦ
flipcards.vars: ΔΦ = Φ_final − Φ_initial, R = total loop resistance
flipcards.tip: Independent of how fast or slow the flux change happens!

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Capacitance of Spherical Capacitor (R₂ > R₁)
flipcards.prompt: Capacitance between concentric spherical shells of inner radius R₁ and outer radius R₂
flipcards.vars: k = 1/(4πε₀), K = dielectric constant (1 for air/vacuum), R₁ = inner radius, R₂ = outer radius
flipcards.tip: Note that k = 1/(4πε₀) is in the denominator; for an isolated sphere (R₂ → ∞), C = 4πε₀KR₁

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Potential Difference Due to Infinite Sheet
flipcards.prompt: Potential difference ΔV between two points at distances R₁ and R₂ from an infinite non-conducting sheet
flipcards.vars: σ = surface charge density, R₁, R₂ = perpendicular distances from the sheet
flipcards.tip: Field E = σ/(2ε₀) is uniform, so ΔV = E · Δr scales linearly with (R₂ − R₁)

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Potential Difference Due to Infinite Line Charge
flipcards.prompt: Potential difference ΔV between radial distances R₁ and R₂ from an infinite line charge (density λ)
flipcards.vars: λ = linear charge density, k = 1/(4πε₀), R₁, R₂ = radial distances from the wire
flipcards.tip: Absolute potential at ∞ is undefined for an infinite line charge; only ΔV between finite R₁, R₂ is defined

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Potential Inside Uniformly Charged Solid Sphere
flipcards.prompt: Electric potential at distance r ≤ R inside a uniformly charged non-conducting solid sphere
flipcards.vars: Q = total charge, R = sphere radius, r = distance from center, k = 1/(4πε₀)
flipcards.tip: At center (r = 0), V_center = 1.5 × V_surface = 3kQ/(2R)

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: SHM Time Period of −q Inside Solid Sphere +Q
flipcards.prompt: Time period of SHM for charge −q (mass m) released inside a tunnel in solid sphere +Q (radius R), and Earth analogy
flipcards.vars: m = particle mass, R = sphere radius, k = 1/(4πε₀), R_E = Earth radius, g = 9.8 m/s²
flipcards.tip: Restoring force F = −(kqQ/R³)r gives ω² = kqQ/(mR³), matching Earth's tunnel SHM (≈ 84.6 min)

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Electric Potential Due to a Dipole
flipcards.prompt: Electric potential at distance r and angle θ from the axis of an electric dipole of moment p
flipcards.vars: p = dipole moment (q·2a), θ = angle between p and position vector r, k = 1/(4πε₀)
flipcards.tip: On equatorial plane (θ = 90°), V = 0 everywhere even though E ≠ 0

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Electric Potential on Axis of Charged Disk
flipcards.prompt: Electric potential at axial distance x from the center of a uniformly charged disk of radius R
flipcards.vars: σ = surface charge density, R = disk radius, x = axial distance from center
flipcards.tip: At the center (x = 0), V = σR/(2ε₀); differentiate −dV/dx to recover the axial E-field

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Self-Potential Energy of Solid & Hollow Sphere
flipcards.prompt: Electrostatic self-energy U of a uniformly charged solid sphere and hollow spherical shell of radius R
flipcards.latex: U_{\text{solid}} = \frac{3 k Q^2}{5 R} \quad | \quad U_{\text{hollow}} = \frac{k Q^2}{2 R}
flipcards.vars: Q = total charge, R = sphere radius, k = 1/(4πε₀)
flipcards.tip: Solid sphere has extra internal field energy (kQ²/10R) compared to hollow shell (kQ²/2R)

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Dipole Moment of Semicircular Charge Distribution
flipcards.prompt: Dipole moment magnitude p for a semicircular/hemispherical geometry with coefficient 8/(3π)
flipcards.vars: q = charge magnitude, R = radius
flipcards.tip: Semicircular plate CM is at 4R/(3π); with opposite charge −q on the other side, separation is 8R/(3π)

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Force Between Two Electric Dipoles
flipcards.prompt: Force between two dipoles p₁, p₂ separated by r in (1) collinear/axial and (2) parallel/broadside alignment
flipcards.latex: F_{\text{axial}} = \frac{6 k p_1 p_2}{r^4} \quad | \quad F_{\text{parallel}} = \frac{3 k p_1 p_2}{r^4}
flipcards.vars: p₁, p₂ = dipole moments, r = center-to-center distance, k = 1/(4πε₀)
flipcards.tip: Force falls off as 1/r⁴; axial (end-on) is double the broadside (parallel) force

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Potential & E-Field at Center of Hemispherical Shell
flipcards.prompt: Electric potential V and electric field E at the center of a uniformly charged hemispherical shell
flipcards.vars: σ = surface charge density, R = radius of hemispherical shell
flipcards.tip: Notice R in V_center = σR/(2ε₀) for voltage units; E_center points along the symmetry axis away from +σ

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Time Period of Displaced Electric Dipole
flipcards.prompt: Time period T of small angular oscillations of a dipole (moment p, inertia I) in uniform field E
flipcards.vars: I = moment of inertia about pivot/CM, p = dipole moment, E = uniform electric field
flipcards.tip: Valid for small angular displacement θ where restoring torque τ = −pE sin θ ≈ −pE θ

flipcards.subject: Physics
flipcards.title: Dipole Moment of Semicircular Ring (+q Arc, −q Base)
flipcards.prompt: Dipole moment of a 180° semicircular ring of radius r with +q on the arc and −q at center/diameter
flipcards.vars: q = charge magnitude, r = radius of semicircular ring
flipcards.tip: Center of charge of a semicircular arc lies at distance 2r/π from the center along the symmetry axis

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: LiAlH4 (LAH) Reduction
flipcards.prompt: Which functional groups are reduced by LiAlH4, and what does it leave untouched?
flipcards.latex: \text{RCHO, RCOR', RCOOH, RCOOR', RCONR}_2, \text{RCN, RNO}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{Alcohols / Amines}
flipcards.vars: Strong nucleophilic hydride donor (H⁻); requires anhydrous ether/THF
flipcards.tip: Does NOT reduce isolated C=C or C≡C (exception: cinnamaldehyde Ph-CH=CH-CHO → Ph-CH=CH-CH2OH)

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: NaBH4 Selective Reduction
flipcards.prompt: Which functional groups are reduced by NaBH4?
flipcards.vars: Mild reducing agent; works in protic solvents (MeOH, EtOH, H2O)
flipcards.tip: Does NOT reduce esters, carboxylic acids, amides, nitriles, or nitro groups

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: DIBAL-H (-78 °C)
flipcards.prompt: What is the role of DIBAL-H at low temperature (-78 °C)?
flipcards.vars: Diisobutylaluminium hydride (bulky electrophilic reducing agent)
flipcards.tip: Stops at the aldehyde stage instead of over-reducing to an alcohol

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Lindlar's Catalyst (H2 / Pd-BaSO4)
flipcards.prompt: Name the products of Lindlar's catalyst with (1) internal alkyne and (2) acyl chloride
flipcards.vars: Pd on BaSO4 poisoned with quinoline or S
flipcards.tip: Gives syn-addition of H2; stops at alkene/aldehyde

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Birch Reduction (Na / liq. NH3)
flipcards.prompt: What does Na / liq. NH3 do to internal alkynes and benzene?
flipcards.vars: Dissolving metal reduction via radical anion
flipcards.tip: Terminal alkynes (RC≡CH) form sodium acetylide (RC≡C⁻Na⁺) + H2↑ instead of alkene

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Clemmensen vs Wolff-Kishner Reduction
flipcards.prompt: Reagents and medium constraints for reducing C=O to CH2
flipcards.vars: Clemmensen = acidic; Wolff–Kishner = strongly basic
flipcards.tip: Use Wolff–Kishner if molecule has acid-sensitive -OH; use Clemmensen if molecule has base-sensitive -X or ester

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Red Phosphorus + HI
flipcards.prompt: What is the effect of Red P + HI on oxygen-containing organic compounds?
flipcards.vars: Most powerful organic reducing agent
flipcards.tip: Glucose + Red P/HI → n-hexane (proves 6-carbon straight chain)

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: PCC (Pyridinium Chlorochromate)
flipcards.prompt: Action of PCC on 1°, 2°, and 3° alcohols
flipcards.vars: Anhydrous Cr(VI) reagent in CH2Cl2
flipcards.tip: Stops 1° alcohol oxidation at the aldehyde (unlike KMnO4 or K2Cr2O7)

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: MnO2 Selective Oxidation
flipcards.prompt: Which alcohols are selectively oxidized by MnO2?
flipcards.vars: Mild heterogeneous oxidant
flipcards.tip: Leaves ordinary saturated 1°/2° alcohols untouched

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Ozonolysis (Reductive vs Oxidative)
flipcards.prompt: Products of O3/Zn-H2O vs O3/H2O2 on alkenes and alkynes
flipcards.vars: Cleaves C=C and C≡C bonds completely
flipcards.tip: Terminal =CH2 gives HCHO in reductive ozonolysis, and CO2 + H2O in oxidative ozonolysis

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: mCPBA (Peroxyacid)
flipcards.prompt: Reactions of mCPBA with alkenes and ketones
flipcards.vars: meta-Chloroperoxybenzoic acid
flipcards.tip: Baeyer–Villiger migratory aptitude: H > 3° > 2° ≈ Ph > 1° > Me

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: HIO4 (Periodic Acid) Cleavage
flipcards.prompt: What bonds are cleaved by HIO4 (Malaprade oxidation)?
flipcards.vars: Also cleaves α-hydroxy ketones and α-diketones
flipcards.tip: 1° alcohol end → HCHO; 2° alcohol end → HCOOH (if flanked by two C-OH groups)

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: SeO2 (Selenium Dioxide)
flipcards.prompt: What are the two signature reactions of SeO2?
flipcards.vars: Oxidizes α-methylene next to C=C or C=O
flipcards.tip: Converts acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) to glyoxal (OHC-CHO)

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: I2 / NaOH (Haloform Test)
flipcards.prompt: Which compounds give a positive iodoform test (yellow CHI3 ppt)?
flipcards.vars: Requires CH3-CO- or CH3-CH(OH)- group
flipcards.tip: Positive for ethanol & ethanal; negative for methanol, methanal, and 3-pentanone

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Tollens' vs Fehling's Reagent
flipcards.prompt: Distinguish Tollens' [Ag(NH3)2]+ and Fehling's (Cu2+ tartrate) selectivity
flipcards.vars: Both oxidize aldehydes to carboxylate ions
flipcards.tip: Tollens' oxidizes BOTH aliphatic and aromatic aldehydes (and HCOOH); Fehling's fails for benzaldehyde

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: SOCl2 vs SOCl2 + Pyridine (Darzen's)
flipcards.prompt: Stereochemical outcome of R-OH + SOCl2 alone vs with pyridine
flipcards.vars: Byproducts SO2↑ and HCl↑ escape as gases
flipcards.tip: Best laboratory method to prepare pure alkyl chlorides

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Alc. KOH vs t-BuOK (Elimination)
flipcards.prompt: Regioselectivity of E2 elimination with alc. KOH vs bulky t-BuOK
flipcards.vars: Both proceed via E2 anti-periplanar elimination
flipcards.tip: Poor leaving groups like -F or -NR3+ also favor Hofmann alkene even with small bases

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: NBS / hν (Allylic/Benzylic Bromination)
flipcards.prompt: Where does NBS (N-bromosuccinimide) substitute in an alkene or alkylbenzene?
flipcards.vars: Provides low steady concentration of Br2 for free-radical substitution
flipcards.tip: Check allylic radical resonance for rearranged minor/major products

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Hydroboration-Oxidation vs Oxymercuration
flipcards.prompt: Compare regioselectivity and stereochemistry of HBO vs OM-DM on alkenes
flipcards.vars: Neither method undergoes carbocation rearrangement
flipcards.tip: Use acid-catalyzed H3O+ only when carbocation rearrangement is expected

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Dil. NaOH vs Conc. NaOH (Carbonyls)
flipcards.prompt: Distinguish Dil. NaOH (Aldol) and Conc. NaOH (Cannizzaro) conditions
flipcards.vars: 50% NaOH drives Cannizzaro disproportionation
flipcards.tip: Exception: (CH3)2CH-CHO has 1 α-H but still gives Cannizzaro with conc. NaOH at high temp

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: CHCl3 + KOH (Two Name Reactions)
flipcards.prompt: What are the two reactions of CHCl3 + KOH with (1) Phenol and (2) 1° Amine?
flipcards.vars: Reactive intermediate is :CCl2 (dichlorocarbene)
flipcards.tip: Carbylamine test is positive ONLY for 1° amines (aliphatic & aromatic), giving foul-smelling isocyanide

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Br2 + KOH (Hofmann Bromamide)
flipcards.prompt: Product and carbon-count change when R-CONH2 reacts with Br2 + KOH
flipcards.vars: Step-down reaction: amine has 1 carbon less than amide
flipcards.tip: Proceeds via isocyanate intermediate with complete retention of stereochemistry

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: NaNO2 + HCl (0–5 °C) on Amines
flipcards.prompt: Compare products of 1° aromatic vs 1° aliphatic vs 2° amines with HNO2
flipcards.vars: 2° amines give yellow oily N-nitrosoamines (R2N-N=O)
flipcards.tip: Aliphatic diazonium salts are unstable even at 0 °C and decompose via carbocation (rearrangement possible)

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Diazonium Salt Reactions (Sandmeyer, H3PO2, HBF4)
flipcards.prompt: Convert ArN2+Cl- to Ar-Cl/Br/CN, Ar-H, and Ar-F
flipcards.vars: ArN2+Cl- + KI (warm) → Ar-I; H2O (warm) → Ar-OH
flipcards.tip: H3PO2 (or EtOH) is the classic deamination reagent to remove -NH2 from a ring

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Hinsberg's Reagent (PhSO2Cl)
flipcards.prompt: How does benzenesulfonyl chloride distinguish 1°, 2°, and 3° amines?
flipcards.vars: 1° sulfonamide has acidic N-H proton, so it dissolves in alkali
flipcards.tip: 2° sulfonamide (PhSO2NR2) has no N-H proton, so it remains insoluble in KOH

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: LiAlH4 + Aldehyde / Ketone
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R-CHO or R-CO-R' + (1) LiAlH4 / dry ether, (2) H3O+
flipcards.vars: Nucleophilic H⁻ attack on carbonyl carbon
flipcards.tip: Works on acyl chlorides (RCOCl → RCH2OH) as well

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: LiAlH4 + Ester (R-COOR')
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R-COOR' + (1) LiAlH4 / ether, (2) H3O+
flipcards.vars: Cleaves the ester into two alcohols
flipcards.tip: Unlike NaBH4, LiAlH4 reduces esters and carboxylic acids (RCOOH → RCH2OH)

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: LiAlH4 + Amide (R-CONH2)
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R-CONH2 + (1) LiAlH4 / ether, (2) H2O
flipcards.vars: Converts C=O of amide into CH2 (same carbon count)
flipcards.tip: Exam trap: gives an AMINE (not an alcohol!). Contrast with Hofmann bromamide (Br2/KOH) which gives 1 C less

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: LiAlH4 + Nitrile (R-CN)
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R-C≡N + (1) LiAlH4 / ether, (2) H2O
flipcards.vars: Complete reduction to 1° amine
flipcards.tip: Isocyanide (R-NC) + LiAlH4 gives a 2° amine (R-NH-CH3)

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: LiAlH4 + Cinnamaldehyde
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: Ph-CH=CH-CHO + (1) LiAlH4 / ether, (2) H3O+
flipcards.vars: Reduces BOTH the conjugated C=C and -CHO
flipcards.tip: Trap: NaBH4 on Ph-CH=CH-CHO reduces only -CHO to give Ph-CH=CH-CH2OH

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: NaBH4 + Aldehyde / Ketone / Acyl Chloride
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R-CHO, R-CO-R', or R-COCl + NaBH4 / MeOH
flipcards.vars: Mild hydride donor; works in protic solvents (MeOH, EtOH, H2O)
flipcards.tip: Selective: reduces -CHO, >C=O, and -COCl without touching C=C

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: NaBH4 + Ester / Acid / Amide / Nitrile
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R-COOR', R-COOH, R-CONH2, or R-CN + NaBH4 / EtOH
flipcards.latex: \text{No Reaction (leaves ester, acid, amide, nitrile untouched)}
flipcards.vars: Used in stepwise synthesis to selectively reduce a ketone in presence of an ester
flipcards.tip: In keto-ester problems, NaBH4 reduces only the ketone; LiAlH4 reduces both

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: DIBAL-H + Ester (-78 °C)
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R-COOR' + (1) DIBAL-H (1 eq, -78 °C), (2) H3O+
flipcards.vars: Low temperature prevents over-reduction to alcohol
flipcards.tip: Key stepwise reagent to convert an ester directly into an aldehyde

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: DIBAL-H + Nitrile (-78 °C)
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R-C≡N + (1) DIBAL-H (-78 °C), (2) H3O+
flipcards.vars: Proceeds via imine intermediate hydrolyzed by H3O+
flipcards.tip: Same outcome as Stephen reduction (SnCl2 + HCl, then H3O+)

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Lindlar's Catalyst + Alkyne
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R-C≡C-R' + H2 / Pd-BaSO4 (quinoline)
flipcards.vars: Syn-addition of H2 on poisoned Pd surface
flipcards.tip: Stops at alkene; does not reduce further to alkane

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Lindlar's Catalyst + Acyl Chloride (Rosenmund)
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R-COCl + H2 / Pd-BaSO4
flipcards.vars: Rosenmund reduction
flipcards.tip: Does not work for H-COCl (formyl chloride is unstable)

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Na / liq. NH3 + Internal Alkyne
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R-C≡C-R' + Na / liq. NH3 (Birch reduction)
flipcards.vars: Anti-addition via radical anion intermediate
flipcards.tip: Contrast with H2/Pd-BaSO4 which gives cis-alkene

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Na / liq. NH3 + Terminal Alkyne
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R-C≡C-H + Na / liq. NH3
flipcards.vars: Acid-base reaction (terminal alkyne H is acidic)
flipcards.tip: Trap: terminal alkynes do NOT reduce to alkenes with Na/NH3; they form acetylide salt for SN2 coupling!

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Na / liq. NH3 / EtOH + Benzene
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: Benzene (or Substituted Benzene) + Na / liq. NH3 + EtOH
flipcards.vars: Unconjugated diene formed
flipcards.tip: EWG (-COOH) stays on the sp² carbon; EDG (-OMe, -Me) stays on the sp² carbon? Check: EDG stays on C=C, EWG goes to CH2!

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Clemmensen Trap (Acid-Sensitive -OH)
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: HO-CH2-CH2-CO-CH3 + Zn-Hg / conc. HCl
flipcards.vars: Strongly acidic medium converts -OH to -Cl
flipcards.tip: To keep -OH intact while reducing C=O → CH2, use Wolff–Kishner (NH2NH2/KOH)

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Wolff-Kishner Trap (Base-Sensitive -Cl)
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: Cl-CH2-CH2-CO-CH3 + NH2NH2 / KOH, glycol, Δ
flipcards.vars: Strongly basic KOH causes E2 dehydrohalogenation of -Cl
flipcards.tip: To keep -Cl intact while reducing C=O → CH2, use Clemmensen (Zn-Hg/HCl)

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: PCC + 1° / 2° Alcohol
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R-CH2-OH (1°) and R-CH(OH)-R' (2°) + PCC / CH2Cl2
flipcards.vars: Anhydrous mild oxidant
flipcards.tip: Stops 1° alcohol at aldehyde; 3° alcohol gives NO reaction

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: KMnO4 / H+ (or K2Cr2O7 / H+) + 1° Alcohol
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R-CH2-OH + KMnO4 / H+ (or K2Cr2O7 / H+)
flipcards.vars: Strong aqueous oxidant oxidizes 1° alcohol all the way to carboxylic acid
flipcards.tip: 2° alcohol still stops at ketone (R-CO-R')

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: KMnO4 / KOH, Δ + Alkylbenzene
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: Ph-CH2-CH3 (or Ph-CH(CH3)2) + KMnO4 / KOH, Δ then H3O+
flipcards.vars: Entire side chain oxidizes to -COOH if ≥ 1 benzylic H is present
flipcards.tip: Trap: tert-butylbenzene Ph-C(CH3)3 has NO benzylic H, so NO reaction!

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: MnO2 + Allylic / Benzylic Alcohol
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: CH2=CH-CH(OH)-CH2-CH2-OH + MnO2
flipcards.vars: Oxidizes ONLY allylic or benzylic -OH
flipcards.tip: Leaves the primary saturated -CH2OH completely untouched

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Reductive Ozonolysis (O3, Zn/H2O) + Alkene
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R-CH=C(R')2 + (1) O3, (2) Zn / H2O
flipcards.vars: Cleave C=C and put =O on each alkene carbon
flipcards.tip: Terminal =CH2 gives formaldehyde (HCHO)

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Oxidative Ozonolysis (O3, H2O2) + Alkene
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R-CH=CH2 + (1) O3, (2) H2O2
flipcards.vars: H2O2 oxidizes aldehydes to carboxylic acids; HCHO → CO2 + H2O
flipcards.tip: Same products as hot KMnO4 / H+ oxidative cleavage

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Ozonolysis + Alkyne
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R-C≡C-R' + (1) O3, (2) H2O (vs Zn/H2O)
flipcards.vars: With H2O only, H2O2 formed in situ cleaves to acids
flipcards.tip: Terminal alkyne R-C≡CH + O3/H2O gives R-COOH + CO2

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: mCPBA + Alkene (Epoxidation)
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: cis-2-butene + mCPBA
flipcards.vars: Stereospecific syn-epoxidation
flipcards.tip: If followed by H3O+ (acidic ring opening), overall product is anti-1,2-diol!

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: mCPBA + Ketone (Baeyer-Villiger)
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: Ph-CO-CH3 + mCPBA
flipcards.vars: Inserts O next to C=O on the side with higher migratory aptitude
flipcards.tip: Migratory aptitude: H > 3° > 2° ≈ Ph > 1° > CH3

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: SOCl2 alone + Chiral Alcohol
flipcards.prompt: Predict stereochemistry: (R)-2-butanol + SOCl2 (no pyridine)
flipcards.vars: Intramolecular nucleophilic substitution (SNi)
flipcards.tip: Gaseous byproducts SO2↑ and HCl↑ drive reaction to completion

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: SOCl2 + Pyridine + Chiral Alcohol
flipcards.prompt: Predict stereochemistry: (R)-2-butanol + SOCl2 + Pyridine
flipcards.vars: Pyridine traps HCl and Cl⁻ attacks from backside (SN2)
flipcards.tip: Notice how adding pyridine flips retention → inversion!

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: aq. KOH vs alc. KOH + Alkyl Halide
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: CH3-CH(Br)-CH2-CH3 + (1) aq. KOH vs (2) alc. KOH, Δ
flipcards.vars: Aqueous favors substitution; alcoholic + heat favors elimination
flipcards.tip: 3° halide + aq. KOH still gives mostly elimination on heating

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: CHCl3 + KOH + Phenol (Reimer-Tiemann)
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: Phenol + CHCl3 + aq. KOH, then H+
flipcards.vars: Electrophile is neutral dichlorocarbene (:CCl2)
flipcards.tip: With CCl4 + KOH instead of CHCl3, product is Salicylic acid

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: CHCl3 + KOH + 1° Amine (Carbylamine)
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R-NH2 (or Ph-NH2) + CHCl3 + alc. KOH, Δ
flipcards.vars: Foul-smelling isocyanide formed
flipcards.tip: 2° and 3° amines do NOT give this test

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: NaNO2 + HCl (0–5 °C) + Aniline
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: Ph-NH2 + NaNO2 + HCl (0–5 °C)
flipcards.vars: Diazotization; stable below 5 °C
flipcards.tip: Above 5 °C (or on warming with H2O), Ph-N2+Cl- hydrolyzes to Phenol + N2↑

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: NaNO2 + HCl + 1° Aliphatic Amine
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: CH3-CH2-CH2-NH2 + NaNO2 + HCl
flipcards.vars: Aliphatic diazonium ion is unstable and loses N2 immediately
flipcards.tip: Trap: n-propylamine gives propan-2-ol (major) due to 1,2-hydride shift in carbocation!

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: NaNO2 + HCl + 2° Amine
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R2NH + NaNO2 + HCl
flipcards.vars: Yellow oily N-nitrosoamine (Liebermann nitroso test)
flipcards.tip: Used to distinguish 2° amines from 1° and 3° amines

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: ArN2+Cl- + CuCl/HCl (Sandmeyer)
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: Ph-N2+Cl- + CuCl/HCl (or CuBr/HBr, CuCN)
flipcards.vars: Gattermann reaction uses Cu powder + HX instead of CuX
flipcards.tip: For Ph-I, no Cu catalyst is needed—just warm with aq. KI

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: ArN2+Cl- + H3PO2 / H2O
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: Ar-N2+Cl- + H3PO2 + H2O (or CH3CH2OH)
flipcards.vars: Reductive deamination of aromatic ring
flipcards.tip: Classic stepwise trick: use -NH2 to direct o/p (e.g. 2,4,6-tribromoaniline), then diazotize + H3PO2 to get 1,3,5-tribromobenzene!

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: ArN2+Cl- + HBF4, Δ (Balz-Schiemann)
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: Ph-N2+Cl- + (1) HBF4, (2) Δ
flipcards.vars: Standard synthesis of aryl fluorides
flipcards.tip: With NaNO2/Cu, Δ on Ph-N2+BF4- gives Nitrobenzene (Ph-NO2)

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: ArN2+Cl- + Phenol (Azo Coupling)
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: Ph-N2+Cl- + Phenol (pH 9–10, 0–5 °C)
flipcards.vars: Electrophilic substitution at para position of phenol
flipcards.tip: Aniline couples at pH 4–5 (weakly acidic) to give yellow p-aminoazobenzene

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Phenol + Br2 / H2O
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: Phenol + Br2 / H2O (bromine water)
flipcards.vars: Phenoxide ion in water is strongly activating
flipcards.tip: Salicylic acid + Br2/H2O also decarboxylates to give 2,4,6-tribromophenol!

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Phenol + Br2 / CS2 (273 K)
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: Phenol + Br2 / CS2 (or CHCl3) at 273 K
flipcards.vars: Non-polar solvent suppresses phenoxide formation → monobromination
flipcards.tip: Same contrast holds for Aniline: Br2/H2O gives 2,4,6-tribromoaniline; protect with Ac2O first for monobromination

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: Amide + Br2 / KOH (Hofmann Bromamide)
flipcards.prompt: Predict product: R-CONH2 + Br2 + 4 KOH
flipcards.vars: 1° amine with 1 carbon LESS than amide
flipcards.tip: Complete retention of stereochemistry at migrating chiral group R

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: R-X + KCN vs AgCN
flipcards.prompt: Compare products: R-Br + KCN (aq/alc) vs R-Br + AgCN
flipcards.vars: Ambident nucleophile CN⁻: KCN is ionic (C-attack); AgCN is covalent (N-attack)
flipcards.tip: In stepwise problems: R-CN + LiAlH4 → 1° amine, whereas R-NC + LiAlH4 → 2° amine!

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: R-X + KNO2 vs AgNO2
flipcards.prompt: Compare products: R-Br + KNO2 vs R-Br + AgNO2
flipcards.vars: KNO2 is ionic (O-attack → alkyl nitrite); AgNO2 is covalent (N-attack → nitroalkane)
flipcards.tip: R-NO2 + Sn/HCl → R-NH2 (1° amine), whereas R-O-N=O hydrolyzes to R-OH

flipcards.subject: Chemistry
flipcards.title: R-OH + PCl5 vs PCl3 vs Red P/I2
flipcards.prompt: Predict products: R-OH + PCl5, PCl3, or Red P + I2
flipcards.vars: Standard halogenation of alcohols
flipcards.tip: Red P + Br2/I2 generates PBr3/PI3 in situ to give R-Br / R-I
